compositionText: Composition and Construction Knit is knitted from high-quality monofilament polypropylene yarn. Polypropylene is a synthetic linear polyolefin, and the mesh is non-absorbable, intended to remain in situ as a permanent implant unless removal is clinically indicated. The mesh is cut to precision with all edges sealed, thermally annealed to help prevent fabric curling, and ultrasonically washed before being packed in internationally accepted, standard medical-grade paper. Its pore structure is designed to support visibility of the surgical field and tissue colonization as the mesh integrates with surrounding tissue. Knit is smooth, soft, strong and flexible, characteristics that support handling and conformability during implantation, and it is designed to minimise patient discomfort. It is available in four variants — Ultra Soft, Soft, Macropore and Robust — allowing the mesh to be matched to the repair, the defect and the surgeon’s preference. Selection of variant, size, configuration and fixation method is at the discretion of the surgeon, based on the patient’s condition, the type and location of the defect, and operative requirements. Knit can be fixed with sutures or tackers. subtitle: 3D Anatomical Polypropylene Mesh
lead: Knit 3D is a sterile, non-absorbable, pre-shaped three-dimensional polypropylene mesh with a contoured anatomical design for laparoscopic inguinal hernia repair, supplied in left and right configurations across three sizes in Macropore and Medium pore.

specs.Instructions for Use: Supplied with every unit; available on request

compositionText: Composition and Construction Knit 3D is knitted from monofilament polypropylene. Polypropylene is a synthetic linear polyolefin, and the mesh is non-absorbable, intended to remain in situ as a permanent implant unless removal is clinically indicated. Rather than a flat sheet, Knit 3D is pre-shaped into a three-dimensional, anatomically contoured form and is supplied in dedicated left and right configurations. It is offered in two pore constructions — Macropore and Medium pore — so the mesh can be matched to the repair and the surgeon’s preference. The pre-shaped, three-dimensional configuration is intended to follow the contours of the inguinal anatomy, to assist secure placement, and to support deployment and positioning during laparoscopic surgery. Selection of pore construction, size, side and fixation method is at the discretion of the surgeon, based on the patient’s condition, the type and location of the defect, and operative requirements. Knit 3D can be fixed with sutures or tackers. Published literature on anatomical, three-dimensional mesh designs describes potential advantages such as anatomical conformity, tissue integration and ease of handling; these relate to the mesh category in general and are not presented as a claim of clinical performance for this device. compositionText: Composition and Construction Tiolene is knitted from monofilament polypropylene, and each fibre is covered by a high-purity, adherent titanium dioxide coating applied by chemical vaporisation of titanium over the polymer mesh. The titanium dioxide surface is intended to improve the biocompatibility of the mesh, and the titanisation process makes the surface hydrophilic. The mesh is supplied in medium-pore and large-pore variants; the large-pore knitted structure is intended to allow seroma drainage. Tiolene is a lightweight, flexible mesh with blue orientation stripes to assist positioning, and it is finished with a laser-cutting process. As a single-layer mesh it does not have a distinct visceral barrier surface. The mesh can be trimmed to suit the repair and fixed with sutures or tackers. Selection of the pore variant, size and fixation method is at the discretion of the surgeon, based on the patient’s condition, the type and location of the defect, and operative requirements. compositionText: Composition and Construction Silene is composed of one layer of polymer matrix for the parietal side and one layer of medical-grade silicone for the visceral side. The polymer matrix is formed of thermally interlaced polymer fibres, and the two functional layers are fused into a single composite mesh. The polymer surface is intended to encourage tissue ingrowth and colonisation on the parietal side, while the non-adherent silicone is intended to act as a barrier and to minimise tissue attachment on the visceral side. The mesh also contains drainage holes intended to allow seroma drainage. The translucent silicone barrier allows visualisation of the underlying tissues and vessels, and the low-profile design is intended to support laparoscopic deployment. The mesh can be trimmed and shaped to suit the repair. Proper orientation is essential: the silicone surface is placed against the bowel or other visceral structures, and the polymer matrix surface faces the tissue plane where ingrowth is intended. Silene is compatible with usual fixation devices, including sutures, helicoidal fixation and tacking devices. Selection of size, orientation and fixation method is at the discretion of the surgeon, based on the patient’s condition, the type and location of the defect, and operative requirements. compositionText: Composition and Construction Teflene is composed of a knitted polypropylene mesh for the parietal side firmly fused to an expanded polytetrafluoroethylene (ePTFE) sheet for the visceral side. Polytetrafluoroethylene is a linear homochain polymer with a carbon backbone saturated with fluorine, an inert fluoropolymer. The macroporous polypropylene surface is intended to encourage tissue ingrowth on the parietal side, while the solid, low-porosity ePTFE sheet is placed against the visceral side and is intended to act as a permanent barrier that minimises tissue attachment. The mesh also contains perforated holes intended to allow drainage of fluid and seroma. A placement marker is provided to assist orientation. Proper orientation is essential: the ePTFE surface is placed against the bowel or other visceral structures, and the polypropylene surface faces the tissue plane where ingrowth is intended. The mesh can be fixed with sutures or tackers, with fixation engaging the mesh rather than the sealed edge alone. Selection of size, orientation and fixation method is at the discretion of the surgeon, based on the patient’s condition, the type and location of the defect, and operative requirements. compositionText: Composition and Construction Duolene is composed of one layer of knitted lightweight polypropylene mesh for the parietal side and one layer of medical-grade polyethylene film for the visceral side. Both functional layers are fused together using a process that does not rely on adhesive. The polypropylene surface is macroporous and is intended to encourage tissue ingrowth on the parietal side, while the extruded, expanded, low-porosity polyethylene film is intended to act as a barrier and to minimise tissue ingrowth and foreign body reaction on the visceral side. The mesh also contains micropores intended to allow seroma drainage. Duolene is transparent, allowing visualisation of the underlying anatomy, and its thin, lightweight design is intended to support rolling and laparoscopic placement. A placement marker is provided to assist orientation. The mesh can be fixed with sutures or tackers. Selection of size, orientation and fixation method is at the discretion of the surgeon, based on the patient’s condition, the type and location of the defect, and operative requirements. compositionText: Composition and Construction Monosolve V2 is a composite of non-absorbable polypropylene and absorbable poliglecaprone 25. The polypropylene component is intended to provide lasting reinforcement and support for the repair, while the poliglecaprone 25 component is gradually resorbed by the body and is fully absorbed within approximately 90 to 120 days, so that less permanent material remains in situ over time. It is supplied as a flat sheet in a range of rectangular and square sizes. Monosolve V2 has a lightweight construction intended to reduce the amount of implanted material and to support conformability with surrounding tissue, while the polypropylene component is intended to provide durable structural support. Selection of size, orientation and fixation method is at the discretion of the surgeon, based on the patient’s condition, the type and location of the defect, and operative requirements. Monosolve V2 can be fixed with sutures or tackers. Published research on composite and semi absorbable mesh systems describes the rationale for combining non-absorbable polypropylene with an absorbable polymer such as poliglecaprone; this relates to the mesh category in general and is not presented as a claim of clinical performance for this device. name: Tacksure
subtitle: Mesh Tacker
lead: TACKSURE Mesh Tacker is a sterile, single-use laparoscopic and open-surgery device for fixing surgical mesh to soft tissue during hernia repair, available with titanium helical or absorbable polyglactin fasteners.

specs.Material: Titanium helical or absorbable PGLA fasteners
specs.Instructions for Use: Supplied with every unit; available on request

compositionText: Composition and Construction The device is constructed from medical-grade polymer and medical-grade stainless steel, with fasteners made of titanium helical tacks and/or polyglactin tacks. This lets TACKSURE be offered in two fastener configurations: a non-absorbable variant with titanised helical fixators that remain in situ unless removal is clinically indicated, and an absorbable variant using screw-shaped polyglactin (PGLA) tacks. Device materials in tissue contact are biocompatible and suitable for their intended use. TACKSURE delivers one fastener per activation, so the surgeon places each fastener deliberately rather than counting on a feed. The housing and trigger put that placement under hand control, and each fastener anchors the mesh mechanically at the point chosen. The device is compatible with a range of surgical meshes, including single-layer and composite or dual-layer types, and suits both laparoscopic and open approaches. Approved indications, and any limits on mesh type, are stated in the instructions for use. TACKSURE is supplied as a disposable 5 mm instrument with a 350 mm shaft length. Configurations include 20 or 30 titanised helical fixators, or 30 absorbable PGLA fixators, allowing fastener type and count to be matched to the mesh, anatomy, and surgical technique.
